class.name: VolumetricCloudMaterial
class.brief_description: Reusable layered noise and density material for native Mode 0 clouds.
class.description: Assign to [member VolumetricCloudEffect.cloud_material]. This dedicated volume material uses a fixed density shader and does not accept arbitrary [Shader] graphs. The material owns noise texture references and density parameters; the effect owns GPU rendering and temporal history. Changing a structural parameter, replacing a texture reference, or receiving a texture's [signal Resource.changed] signal invalidates cloud history. When updating an [ImageTexture3D] in place, call [method Resource.emit_changed] afterward because its update method does not emit that signal automatically. Saving, loading, and duplicating this Resource does not require a RenderingDevice. Textures contain linear data, sampled with repeat addressing and trilinear filtering. Supply complete offline mip chains. The density shader chooses mip level from ray-step length and pixel footprint. High-frequency erosion fades when it cannot be sampled reliably; sunlight shadow marches use the coarser body shape. Texture generation is not performed each frame. Without a body texture, a procedural body is used. Without a detail texture, detail erosion is skipped. Without a weather map, global coverage is spatially constant. No regional cloud volumes or multiple-scattering features are introduced. The cyclic density model replaces the legacy body and erosion equation with a baked recursively warped cyclic field. Broad structure changes local bottom and top heights, while the full octave field and optional residual preserve continuous interior density. This material does not generate the baked field. A cyclic material without a valid cyclic texture explicitly falls back to the legacy model. A continuous hashed world-space macro field varies the cyclic domain, global layout, and local heights without repeating the volume texture's tile period. Its four corner values are interpolated smoothly, and the domain Jacobian expands the mip footprint where needed. This adds arithmetic, not texture samples, authored cloud volumes, or regional state. Cyclic volume sampling uses an equilateral world-XZ triangle grid. Each vertex hashes a continuous yaw, scale, and 3D texture offset; three volume samples blend with continuous barycentric weights. Centered variance compensation prevents the blend from collapsing toward a uniform mean. The same three RGBA samples supply body, internal detail, and local height, including the sunlight march. No additional detail-volume fetch is added. Coverage and density support continuous updates without clearing all history. Texture, density-model, profile, scale, erosion and albedo edits invalidate history through a structural version; abrupt coverage/density changes are rejected per rendered view.

members.member: Selects the density equation. See [enum DensityModel].

Linear RGBA cyclic field with complete offline mips. R contains the broad octave sum, G the complete octave sum, B a normalized high-frequency residual centered at 0.5, and A an independent low-frequency height field. All channels are in [0,1]. Used only by [constant DENSITY_MODEL_CYCLIC].
High-frequency cyclic residual strength in [0,1]. Filtered by the ray-step and pixel footprint; omitted from the four-step sunlight march.
Local bottom and top variation as a fraction of layer thickness, in [0,0.6]. Local envelopes remain bounded by the global spherical layer.
Exponent applied to the continuous cyclic density ramp, in [0.1,4]. Larger values reduce low-density wisps while preserving dense interiors.
RGBA body volume. R contains a sparse Perlin-Worley body, G/B/A contain inverted Worley F1 at increasing frequencies (reference assets use 4/8/16 cells per tile).
RGB inverted Worley F1 at increasing frequencies. Channels are weighted 0.625/0.25/0.125. Alpha is unused. Detail primarily erodes the body boundary.
Optional globally tiled layout map; R modulates cloud coverage. Other channels are unused. This is not a regional weather volume.
Coverage in [0,1], mapped to the selected density distribution. Zero removes clouds.

World-space meters per body texture tile. The cyclic model bends the horizontal coordinates with a broad field and uses 2.5 times the vertical frequency to retain depth variation within the cloud layer.

Legacy erosion texture tile size in meters. In cyclic mode it controls the sample-footprint threshold for fading the baked B-channel residual; that residual shares the body samples, so its spatial frequencies follow shape_scale and the baked octaves.
World-space meters per layout texture tile.
Legacy-model boundary erosion strength in [0,1]. Dense cloud interiors are protected from uniform noisy thinning. Not used by the cyclic model.
Density transition width above the coverage threshold. Smaller values produce firmer silhouettes.
Normalized base fade start/end and top fade start/end. Values must satisfy 0 ≤ x < y ≤ z < w ≤ 1.
Linear single-scattering albedo. RGB is clamped to [0,1]; alpha is unused.

constants.constant: Legacy Perlin-Worley body and Worley boundary erosion.
Baked recursive cyclic structure with locally varying heights and continuous interior density.
